EXPERIMENT: the SAME bytes, the SAME code, six different file-iteration orders
WHY: current_pressure.denominator_guard builds den[id_survey] while iterating an UNSORTED glob.glob(). id_survey is not unique across the archive (14,649 keys appear in more than one season file; 2,443 carry conflicting values; 1,759 of those conflicts flip DROP vs KEEP). Whichever file the filesystem hands over LAST wins the key, so the published numbers are a property of the directory listing order of the machine that ran it.
METHOD: glob.glob is replaced, for the duration of one process, by a deterministic shuffle with a fixed seed. Nothing in ENGINE/ or CASES/ is edited. This is exactly what a different filesystem does to the shipped code.
SCRIPT: CERT-V2/p1_drift_cause.py (asc/desc) and the six-seed shuffle recorded here
FINDING: The committed value 0.918 was not reproduced by ANY of the eight orders tried, including the two extreme ones. It is not a property of the data; it is a property of the machine that produced it. The published headline number for the one cell that qualifies -- 'ESTABILIDADE 0.918' in FINAL-DELIVERY-A-R.md section L -- is therefore not reproducible from this repository.
SCOPE_OF_THE_DEFECT: Only OLIVO declares DENOMINATOR_VAR, and only OLIVO drifted. VITE reproduced to the digit (0.596 stability, 0.806 dominant share) under every order. The defect is in the denominator join, not in the pressure definition.

TWO_SEPARATE_BUGS.JOIN_KEY_NOT_UNIQUE: id_survey repeats across season files, so even under a FIXED order the denominator joined to a visit can come from a different season. This one is wrong in every order and is the more serious of the two.
